taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 0 state changes, each allowed by a review (0 reviews in all)
1 phase had the tools designed for them

finalText:
All twelve status codes are defined in RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics), section 15. I opened it at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html and read each code's own section. I did not open RFC 9111 (HTTP Caching).

Heuristic cacheability here means the section says "A NNN response is heuristically cacheable". Five codes have no such statement in their sections, so I marked them false: 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422. The other seven do state it: 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501.

The specification's reason phrases differ from the older names for two codes. 413 is "Content Too Large" (it was "Payload Too Large" in RFC 7231). 422 is "Unprocessable Content".

I found no conflicts between the task, the sources and the domain rules. The sources did not disagree with each other.
